say: Leading responsible AI use in your team.
This is the video for module 3 of AI Literacy.

The wrong response is to start with tools. The right response is to start with their work.

say: Even unpaid work has costs, so cost before you price. For example, Folake is asked to run a one-day workshop for 20 members of a market women's association.
She counts 14 hours for preparation, delivery and follow-up, and values her time at 5,000 naira an hour. That is 70,000 naira.
Printing is about 8,000 naira, transport about 6,000 and data about 3,000. Her direct costs are 17,000 naira.
The total is 87,000 naira, or 4,350 naira per participant. She quotes 90,000 naira for the day.
If the group cannot pay, she knows exactly what to ask a sponsor for.
Write a short proposal: purpose, deliverables, exclusions, responsibilities, timeline, price, and how success will be checked.
Promise skills you can measure, not claims that AI will double productivity.

panel.heading: Agree it in writing
left: Exclusions: what you will not do
right: Confirm money in your account app

say: When someone asks for more, like a Facebook page or a grant, check it against the proposal. If it is out of scope, offer a separate price.
Take payment by traceable transfer and confirm it in your account app. Screenshots of transfers can be faked.

say: A one-page policy prevents leaked data and confusion. Start with its purpose, and which official apps are approved.

panel.heading: Seven parts of a one-page policy
items: Purpose and approved tools
Allowed uses: drafts, summaries, ideas
Not allowed: decisions about people
Data rules: no names, IDs or health data
Human review, disclosure, review date

say: List the allowed uses, like first drafts, summaries and training materials.

say: Never create or share AI images, video or voice of a real person without their clear permission. It can cause serious harm and may break the law.

panel.heading: When things go wrong

cards.d: Never create AI images, video or voice of a real person without clear permission.
Find out what happened. Delete the chat, correct the message, tell those who got it.
Tell your data protection lead, who checks what the Data Protection Act 2023 requires.

say: If someone breaks the policy, respond calmly. The aim is to learn, not to shame. Find out what happened, correct it, and tell anyone who received wrong information.

say: If other people's personal data was exposed, tell the person responsible for data protection. Then record the incident and the fix.

say: To remember. Start with the work, not the tools. Keep high-risk decisions human. Cost your time and every expense. Agree scope and payment in writing. And give your team a one-page policy.
